About Me

I am a Ph.D. student in Transportation Engineering at Rutgers University New Brunswick. My research interests include Intelligent Transportation System, Transportation IoT, and Machine Learning.

Experience

Center for Advanced Infrastructure and Transportation

Graduate Research Assistant - Sept. 2021 - Present

Developing edge-end, back-end, and front-end.

  • Developed a real-time passenger railcar positioning tool for both web display and onboard display.
  • Initiated the design and development of a multiprocessing edge server to read and decode data from onboard sensors for efficient storage to MySQL and InfluxDB, fuse data on the edge via MQTT, and send the solution to cloud.
  • Engineered and implemented a backend server on AWS EC2 capable of receiving and processing real-time data from edge servers distributed across various vehicles.
  • Developed a WebSocket server to enable real-time communication with connected browsers for instant updates of the vehicles’ status.
  • Developed RESTful APIs using Python Flask Framework to allow users to query past data from MySQL or InfluxDB.
  • Built a web-based dashboard for tracking the vehicles on a map, real-time multi-camera viewing, and graphing various performance metrics using HTML/CSS, JavaScript, and ArcGIS API served on AWS EC2 with Nginx.
  • Engineered a video streaming feature using FFmpeg to convert the RTSP stream to HLS and stream the video to web browser with hls.js.
  • Established monitoring tools using Telegraf, Grafana, and AWS CloudWatch to monitor edge status and track server performance, identifying bottlenecks and optimizing resource utilization.
  • Dockerized various server applications and utilized Docker Compose for orchestrating multi-container applications, enhancing deployment consistency and portability
  • Designed and trained an XGBoost model to predict signal equipment failures in the next month using past inspection and maintenance data giving an AUC of 74%.
  • Built an interactive web application for risk and resilience analysis of transportation infrastructure using Python Flask framework and ArcGIS JavaScript API.

Risk and Resilience Analysis Web Tool

  • Developed a map-based tool to estimate and visualize flood risks for all segments in the roadway network considering various future sea level rise scenarios.
  • Output risk levels are shown on the map by three color scales
  • Detailed input data and output risk values are shown on the road info page by clicking on/selecting the specific segment
  • Editable input parameters of each road segment within the roadway info page
  • Global parameters can be updated at once across the network from a side widget
  • Dataset including output risks is exportable as a CSV/HTML file
